about: Each reviewed change to the extension's security baseline (#21 slice 1b): the CSP, the permissions, the destination registry, the network ledger, and the sources that hold the network rules. npm run check:security-baseline, which the build runs, fails unless the latest entry records the tree as it is, names each part that changed since the entry before it in its files, its issue, and why each change was made. npm run check:security-baseline -- --print prints the digest and parts for a new entry.

entries.summary: The first baseline: the CSP written out with declared fixes, the permissions as 1.4.0 has them, the destination registry, the network ledger, and the sources that hold the network rules.

rationale.why: A resource type no directive names falls back to the package only, instead of anywhere.
No page embeds a plugin object; 'self' allowed one from the package.
No page sets a <base>, so a script can't move where relative URLs resolve.
No page submits a form to a URL, so a form can't send its fields anywhere.
Video blocks embed these two players and nothing else frames into a page.

Written out because default-src 'self' would block them: image blocks load from any web address, favicons come from Google's service, and pasted and stored images are data: and blob: URLs, as in 1.4.0.
Written out with default-src 'self': media is the package's or the user's own.
Written out with default-src 'self'. 'unsafe-inline' stays until #16's counts of style attributes and <style> blocks reach zero, and the check fails once they do.
Written out with default-src 'self': fonts are the package's or inlined.
A declared fix: an Ollama URL on 127.0.0.1 is the same local server as localhost, which 1.4.0's CSP reached and this address didn't. No new host permission: Ollama answers with its own CORS headers.

rationale.change: script-src 'self' 'wasm-unsafe-eval', and connect-src's other sources, unchanged
rationale.why: As 1.4.0: the package's scripts and the embedding runtime's WebAssembly, and the registry's fetch destinations. connect-src isn't widened for a remote WebDAV server: that row's replacement is #19's.

rationale.change: permissions, host permissions and the offscreen reason recorded in security/permissions.json
rationale.why: The set stays 1.4.0's: no new install warning.

rationale.change: the rest of the manifest recorded, its name, description, version and icons aside
rationale.why: A key outside the CSP and the permissions, such as a content script, a web-accessible resource, a sandbox CSP or the service worker's entry, changes what the extension may do as much as they do.

rationale.change: the offscreen document's reasons recorded wherever a script creates it
rationale.why: Each reason is a capability the document is given, and security/permissions.json names each with its issue.

rationale.change: the destination registry, the network ledger, and every module that runs before the guard (the destination client, the rows it imports and its rules, the network guard, its installer, the module that installs it first, its refusal reports and the pages' guard entry), the proxy policy, the worker's network module and the offscreen document recorded
rationale.why: A change to where the extension may connect, or to the code that decides it, needs an entry that says why. The worker's network is a module of its own, which js/background.js installs in one call, so the rest of the worker changes with no entry.
